vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: naver-blog-writer
Version: 0.3.0

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its reliance on executing unprovided local scripts (`tools/preflight`, `tools/setup_runner`, `tools/publish` in SKILL.md) and its use of `npx` to download and execute an external npm package (`@y80163442/naver-thin-runner` in SKILL.md). These practices introduce significant supply chain risks and blind execution vulnerabilities, as the actual code being run from these sources is unknown and could potentially perform arbitrary malicious actions, including data exfiltration or persistence, without explicit instructions within the provided files.

llm.summary: The SKILL.md describes a plausible Naver blog publishing flow, but the published metadata omits many required environment variables and binaries and the runtime instructs running third-party code (npx) and local tools that are not provided — these inconsistencies deserve caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (publishing Naver Blog via ACP/offerings) is coherent with the actions described (preflight, setup_runner, publish, offering execute or control-plane dispatch). However, the registry metadata claims no required env vars or binaries while SKILL.md lists many required environment variables (X_LOCAL_TOKEN, PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, etc.) and tools (tools/preflight, tools/setup_runner, tools/publish, and an npm package). That mismatch is an important inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to run local helper binaries (tools/preflight, tools/setup_runner, tools/publish) and to invoke an npm package via npx (@y80163442/naver-thin-runner). They require human login and access to local daemon endpoints and seal/job endpoints. The steps stay within the publishing purpose, but they instruct executing third-party code and accessing multiple tokens/URLs; the skill also assumes binaries exist even though none are packaged or declared.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which reduces some risk, but the SKILL.md expects local helper binaries and uses npx to run an external npm package. npx will fetch and execute code from the npm registry at runtime — a moderate risk if you haven't audited the package. Also, the skill provides no packaged tools; it's unclear where tools/* come from.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md requires multiple sensitive values (local daemon token X_LOCAL_TOKEN, PROOF_TOKEN/SETUP_ISSUE_URL or SETUP_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, CONTROL_PLANE_URL). Those values are plausible for offering execution or control-plane dispatch, but the registry metadata declares no required env vars — a mismatch. In particular, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY is high privilege; only provide it if absolutely necessary and after verifying the exact flow. The skill does not justify why both offering-execute and admin API creds might be needed concurrently.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true and does not request system-wide changes in the metadata. It instructs running a long-lived local daemon (npx ... start) which is expected for a local runner; that is a runtime behavior rather than a privilege escalation in the registry. Autonomous invocation is enabled by default (normal for skills) but combine that with the credential and code-execution concerns above before enabling broad use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or using this skill: 1) Ask the publisher to correct the registry metadata so required environment variables and required binaries/tools are declared explicitly. 2) Verify the origin and contents of the tools referenced (tools/preflight, tools/setup_runner, tools/publish) — they are not included in the package; do not run unknown local binaries. 3) Audit the npm package @y80163442/naver-thin-runner (review its source on npm/GitHub) before allowing npx to execute it, since npx fetches and runs remote code. 4) Provide the least-privilege credentials: prefer the offering-execute path (OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL + core API key) over supplying a high-privilege ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY; never hand over admin creds unless you trust the implementer. 5) Be aware this workflow starts a long-lived local daemon and requires a one-time human login — plan for where tokens/credentials will be stored locally. If the publisher cannot explain the missing metadata or provide audited tooling, treat the skill as untrusted.
